title: Security Deposit Waiver Bases by Deposit Kind
content:
Each Security Deposit kind offers its own set of waiver bases, its own request window and its own rule on who may record a waiver. A 0 in a window or months column means the basis or the waiver is not offered for that kind.

| Security Deposit kind | Waiver request window (calendar days after assessment) | Prior electric utility letter of credit reference: months of satisfactory payment shown | Closed Lakeshore agreement ended within the last 12 months: months of satisfactory payment | Current income qualification waives | Senior age at or above which the deposit is waived (no balance owed on any agreement) | Medical certification on the agreement in active status waives | Customer care agent may record the waiver |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Residential New Service Deposit | 30 | 12 | 12 | Yes | 65 | Yes | Yes |
| Residential Reestablishment Deposit | 30 | 0 | 0 | No | 0 | Yes | Yes |
| Residential Unauthorized Use Deposit | 0 | 0 | 0 | No | 0 | No | No |
| Small Commercial Service Deposit | 30 | 24 | 24 | No | 0 | No | Yes |
| Medium Commercial Service Deposit | 30 | 24 | 24 | No | 0 | No | Yes |
| Large Power Service Deposit | 0 | 0 | 0 | No | 0 | No | No |

## Keys to the matrix

- **Waiver request window**: calendar days after assessment within which the customer may establish a waiver basis; 0 means the deposit cannot be waived.
- **Prior electric utility letter**: months of satisfactory payment that a letter of credit reference from the customer's prior electric utility must show to waive the deposit; 0 means this waiver is not offered.
- **Closed Lakeshore agreement**: months of satisfactory payment on a closed Lakeshore agreement of the customer, ended within the last 12 months, that waive the deposit; 0 means not offered.
- **Senior age**: the age of the residential account holder at or above which the deposit is waived when no balance is owed on any of the customer's agreements; 0 means not offered.
- **Agent may record**: whether a customer care agent may record the waiver, as opposed to the credit department.

## Points of judgement

- A Residential Reestablishment Deposit can be waived only on a medical certification on the agreement in active status; the letter, prior-history, income and senior-age bases show 0 or No for that kind.
- A Small Commercial Service Deposit can be waived on a prior utility letter or a closed Lakeshore agreement showing 24 months of satisfactory payment; 12 months is not enough for that kind.
- A Residential New Service Deposit is waived for an account holder aged 65 with no balance owed on any of the customer's agreements; at 64 the senior-age basis is not met.
- The Residential Unauthorized Use Deposit and the Large Power Service Deposit show a window of 0 and offer no basis: they cannot be waived, and a customer care agent does not record a waiver for either.
